Lemma
[Second space derivatives of a parametrix convolution] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0263, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0264, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0265, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0266, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0267, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0268, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0269, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0270 ↗ lem:chow-iii-ch23-first-convolution-derivative 1. ch23:23.27\group Convolution differentiation

If $B(x,\operatorname {inj}(g)/2)$ lies in a coordinate chart, then $P_N*G$ is $C^2$ at $x$ and \[ \partial _{x^i}\partial _{x^j}(P_N*G)=\int _0^t\int _{\mathcal M} \partial _{x^i}\partial _{x^j}P_N(x,z,t-s)G(z,y,s)\, d\mu (z)\, ds. \]
Proof

\sketch The difference between $x$- and $z$-second derivatives of $P_N$ is bounded by $C(1+d^2/(t-s))(t-s)^{-n/2}e^{-d^2/4(t-s)}$, hence is integrable. Integrate the $z$-derivative term by parts; its first derivative satisfies the integrable bound used in Lemma 3. Applying the same difference-quotient argument proves the formula.

□
